items.t: Said he believes President Trump is the greatest President for the American worker and job creator.
items.q: I believe President Trump is the greatest President for the American worker and job creator.

items.t: Said his mission is to make sure American workers have the skills and resources to seize new job opportunities.

items.t: Said President Trump is driving an industrial renaissance after years of decline under the previous administration.

items.t: Issued an opinion letter concluding that the service providers of an unnamed online platform were independent contractors, not employees.
items.q: In a 10-page opinion letter dated April 29, Keith Sonderling, the acting administrator of the Labor Department’s wage and hour division, tells the representative of an unnamed online platform that based on a six-factor test, “we conclude that your client’s service providers are independent contractors, not employees of your client.”

items.t: Said the American labor market is the strongest it has been in more than half a century.

items.t: Said the Working Families Tax Cuts let American workers keep more of what they earn.
items.q: American workers are keeping more of what they earn while businesses have the certainty to invest and hire

record.t: Was sworn in as the 31st U.S. Secretary of Labor in the Oval Office, after leading the department as Acting Secretary since April 2026.
record.q: Keith Sonderling was sworn in today as the 31st U.S. Secretary of Labor during a ceremony administered by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in the Oval Office.

record.t: Was named, with Kevin Hassett and Andrea Lucas, to a committee to investigate allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.
record.q: the Committee shall investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is ‘cause’ for Governor Cook’s removal.” The committee will include Kevin Hassett, Trump’s chief economic aide; Keith Sonderling, acting head of the Office of Government Ethics; and Andrea Lucas

record.t: Was confirmed by the Senate as Secretary of Labor by a vote of 47-41.
record.q: Keith Sonderling, of Florida, to be Secretary of Labor Vote Counts: YEAs 47 NAYs 41

record.t: Announced a Labor Day round of opinion letters and guidance from 10 Labor Department agencies on wage, union-election and veterans' re-employment law.
record.q: announced its latest round of opinion letters and ongoing policy efforts to provide greater guidance and transparency to support American workers, job creators, and retirees

record.office: Acting Director, U.S. Office of Government Ethics
record.t: Was designated by President Trump as Acting Director of the U.S. Office of Government Ethics, a post he holds alongside his Labor Department role.
record.q: In June 2026, President Trump designated Sonderling as Acting Director of the U.S. Office of Government Ethics

record.office: Acting Director, Institute of Museum and Library Services
record.t: Was appointed by President Donald J. Trump as Acting Director of the Institute of Museum and Library Services.
record.q: Deputy Secretary of Labor Keith E. Sonderling was sworn in as Acting Director of the Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS) today, after being appointed to the role by President Donald J. Trump.

record.t: Was confirmed by the Senate as Deputy Secretary of Labor by a 53-46 party-line vote.
record.q: The Senate confirmed the nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Deputy Secretary of Labor by a vote of 53-46, party line.

record.office: Leader, Department of Labor transition team
record.t: Led President Trump's Department of Labor transition team before returning to the department in January 2025.
record.q: Sonderling led President Trump’s Department of Labor transition team before returning to the Department in January 2025.

record.office: Acting Under Secretary of Commerce for Minority Business Development
record.t: Served as Acting Under Secretary of Commerce for Minority Business Development in 2025.
record.q: Acting Under Secretary of Commerce for Minority Business Development in 2025

record.t: Was confirmed by the Senate on September 22, 2020 by a vote of 52-41 as Commissioner of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and was sworn in (2020).
record.q: Keith E. Sonderling was sworn in today as Commissioner of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), the agency announced this morning.  Sonderling was nominated by President Trump on July 17, 2019, re-nominated on March 16, 2020, and was confirmed on September 22, 2020 by a Senate vote of 52-41
